page: UpCloud GPU-24xCPU-240GB-1xB200 is a GPU-accelerated virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8570 processor with 24 physical cores and 24 vCPUs operating at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 240.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 10.0 GB per core. Acceleration is driven by a single NVIDIA Blackwell B200 GPU featuring 192 GB of dedicated VRAM.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong performance across multiple domains, particularly in memory bandwidth and specialized instruction sets. The server achieved a PassMark CPU score of 52,754.5 and demonstrated top-tier LLM inference capabilities, processing 9,953.26 tokens per second for prompt processing and 525.92 tokens per second for text generation using a small 135M model. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, reaching 4,156.98 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 251.17 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. Single-core and multi-core CPU performance via stress-ng fall within the average tier, reflecting the 2.0 GHz clock speed and shared CPU allocation.

From an architectural standpoint, this server represents a high-density resource profile optimized for massive parallel workloads. However, certain tradeoffs exist: the CPU allocation is shared, and the instance includes no local storage, meaning external storage solutions must be configured. Qualitatively, the hardware profile offers high cost efficiency for GPU-intensive and memory-heavy workloads by bundling a top-tier Blackwell GPU with substantial system memory, avoiding the need to provision larger, more expensive multi-GPU nodes.

This configuration is highly suited for large language model inference, deep learning training, data science pipelines, and high-performance database operations. The inclusion of advanced CPU instruction sets, such as Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512, further enhances its suitability for mixed AI and vector-processing workloads.
